do_more: Focus on observable human behavior and body language (e.g., facial expressions, emotions, instinctual habits) over abstract historical trivia.
Structure videos around direct excerpt readings or structured episodic reading parts (e.g., 'Watching expression · Reading 5') rather than high-level book summaries.
Target ultra-short video lengths (under 20-30 seconds) to maximize completion rate and push loop re-watches over 100%.
avoid: Avoid generic clickbait hooks stuffed with emojis (e.g., 'The hidden force controlling...', 'Why you buy things... 💸').
Avoid academic book review framing like 'The Book That Changed Psychology' or author-centric history ('Victorian Streets', 'Galton's Classic').
Avoid publishing videos without clear audio/visual retention anchors that lead to immediate drop-off (0% retention).
short.title_style: Clean, authoritative titles using the exact classic book name paired with a specific sub-topic or reading part perform significantly better than emoji-laden clickbait questions.
next_tests: Test a 15-second loop format featuring a single fascinating Darwin observation on facial expression with bold on-screen subtitles.
Test an explicit visual command title (e.g., 'Look closely at this expression from Darwin...') against the standard book title format.
Compare retention and VPD between a 20-second tight excerpt reading and a 45-second narrated insight from 'The Principles of Psychology'.
short.best_title: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals · Watching expression · Reading 5
